name: Muḥyī al-Dīn Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Kāfiyajī
summary: Anatolian Ḥanafī scholar who taught in Cairo and was named after al-Kāfiya, which he read and taught so often; al-Suyūṭī's teacher for fourteen years.
bio: Al-Kāfiyajī was born in Anatolia around 788/1386, studied there and in the East, and came to Cairo, where he taught at the Shaykhūniyya and other madrasas until his death in 879/1474. His name, 'the man of al-Kāfiya', in the Turkish manner, comes from Ibn al-Ḥājib's handbook, which he read and taught again and again.
He wrote on grammar, law, theology and the writing of history; al-Suyūṭī, who studied with him for fourteen years, speaks of him as his chief teacher.
